children: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company (Masdar) said its operating projects generated 40.2 terawatt-hours (TWh) of clean electricity in 2025, up 38 percent from the previous year, avoiding 19.5 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent.
The company increased capacity from projects in operation or under construction by approximately 40 percent from 32 gigawatts (GW) to 45.8 GW.
A further 20.7 GW of secured projects, or projects approaching final investment approval, brought the total portfolio to 66.5 GW by the end of 2025, according to Masdar’s 13th sustainability report.

The 2025 report covered operating platforms across Spain, Portugal and South Eastern and Central Europe, adding wind and solar assets alongside a development pipeline that includes pumped hydro storage.

The company began generating power from the 476 MW Baltic Eagle Offshore Wind Farm in Germany, inaugurated the 250 megawatt (MW) Nur Bukhara solar project in Uzbekistan, and secured financing for the 2 GW Al Sadawi solar project in Saudi Arabia.

Masdar also broke ground on its world-first gigascale round-the-clock clean energy project in Abu Dhabi. Combining a 5.2 GW solar plant with a 19 GWh battery storage system, the project is designed to deliver 1GW of clean power around the clock.

Following the updated Green Finance Framework in March, the company issued a further $1 billion green bond in May as investor orders reached $6.6 billion, with international investors purchasing 85 percent of the bonds.
The issuance brought the total value of Masdar’s outstanding green bonds to $2.75 billion.
Women represented 30.2 percent of the workforce and 20 percent of management roles, while the Emiratisation rate was almost 46 percent, excluding international operations, the report said.

title: Masdar operating projects generate 38% more clean electricity in 2025
